newsitem.title: UK: European beet crop prospects seen mixed on weather.
newsitem.headline: European beet crop prospects seen mixed on weather.

text.p: Improved weather in West European beet growing areas has improved 1996/97 crop prospects, but adverse conditions in East Europe continue to hamper progress, Czarnikow Sugar said in its latest report on Thursday. "In general the weather has improved earlier this year than last, giving beet more time to put on weight and then build sugar content," the report said.

Although there were still some areas such as north Germany which could benefit from more moisture, the weather in August had enabled most West European beet crops to make up some of the ground lost during the early stages of the season, it added.
"For many of the EU countries the development in sugar per hectare terms has shown good improvements, parallel with or better than previous seasons," Czarnikow said.
But two main exceptions were Belgium and France, where growth rates have not been as steep as in other years.
Britain, Germany, Denmark, Sweden and Ireland were all showing good growth rates compared with previous seasons, although at differing levels, the report said.

It added that the weather during the harvest itself would still have a major bearing on the eventual outcome, especially with some of the longer running campaigns such as Britain. The picture was not so bright in Eastern Europe, where a lack of inputs and poor organisation were key factors that could amplify the impact of poor weather, Czarnikow said.
"Despite the better progress that good weather has brought to western Europe there has not been the same optimism for late improvements in the east," it said.

"In both the Ukraine and Russia the summer has been dry but the lack of resources to provide counter-measures has meant that these conditions cause far greater damage than in an equivalent western context."
Delays had been occurring in many Russian growing areas and the additional rains that were forecast were expected to hamper fieldwork although could still be beneficial to the crop.
Poland, the region's third largest producer, was likely to generate a surplus following substantial area gains.
